title: Built a CS-Style Surf/Bhop Game Using AI. Is It Actually Fun?
author: jukevibe
selftext:
I've spent way too much time building a browser game using ChatGPT, and I'm starting to wonder if I've created something genuinely fun or just found an incredibly time-consuming new hobby. 😂

The game is called **JukeVibe**, and it's inspired by the old Counter-Strike 1.6 Hide & Seek servers I used to enjoy.

The basic premise is movement-based tag. Runners try to survive while Chasers hunt them down with knives. Once tagged, you become a Chaser. The real focus is the movement, with CS-style bunny hopping, air strafing, surfing, and momentum-based mechanics.

**The AI development experience has been pretty wild.**

I've been using ChatGPT to help build the game in Three.js, going back and forth with screenshots, testing changes, describing what feels wrong, and iterating constantly.

One of the most interesting things I've learned is that AI can get you surprisingly far, but it can also create an endless cycle of fixing one thing while breaking three others.

I've had entire sections of the map disappear while trying to make seemingly unrelated changes. I've spent ridiculous amounts of time adjusting movement physics, collision detection, character animations, and performance.

And the bigger the project gets, the harder it seems to become to make changes without introducing new problems.

On the other hand, I've managed to build something I probably never would have attempted otherwise. There's a full neighborhood map, surf ramps, bunny hopping, animated characters, different game modes, and multiplayer functionality.

**The biggest challenge right now is optimization.** I've been developing on an older Ryzen 5 2600 / RX 580 setup, and I'm curious how the game performs on more powerful PCs.

I'm also at the point where I've played it so much that I genuinely have no idea whether other people would find it entertaining.

There's still a ton to do, and I'm trying to decide whether it's worth continuing or if I should call it a fun experiment.

**I'd love to hear from others using AI to develop games:**

Have you found that AI-assisted development becomes increasingly difficult as your projects grow? How do you prevent new changes from breaking existing features?

And if anyone wants to actually playtest JukeVibe, send me a DM and I'll share the link. It's free, runs directly in your browser, and requires no installation.

I'd especially appreciate feedback on FPS, movement mechanics, and whether the gameplay is genuinely fun.

I'm not looking for compliments. If it sucks, I'd rather know now than spend another 200 hours working on it. 😂
